title: Standardized protocol and outcome measurements for the collagen antibody-induced arthritis mouse model
protocol: Prepare a monoclonal antibody cocktail for intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection.
Inject the monoclonal antibody cocktail on day 0 into each mouse.
Intraperitoneally inject LPS on day 3 into each mouse.
Place the mouse on a metal grid to ensure it can grip with all four paws.
Hold the tail of the mouse as close to its body as possible with your dominant hand.
Provide syringes and needles according to the number of animals to be injected.
Use ice to thaw the CAIA antibody cocktail.
Disinfect surfaces with alcohol.
Equip a spare cage as a recovery cage following injections.
Equip a standard cage for experimental animals with nesting material, food, and drinking water enriched with analgesic metamizole.
Hold the mouse with the abdomen facing upwards at a 45° angle and the head towards the table.
Aim for the lower right abdomen with the needle directed towards the thorax at a 30°–40° angle.
Perforate the skin and slowly aspirate.
Check the syringe for any aspirated liquid.
Only apply the antibody cocktail if no liquids are aspirated.
Wait 5 seconds after application before slowly removing the needle and syringe.
Check health status and body weight daily.
Conduct daily body weight assessment using a regular laboratory scale and glass container.
Assess clinical arthritis employing the semquantitative arthritis score.
Score each paw between 0-3 based on swelling and erythema.
Place front and back paws on scale paper to document arthritis severity.
Measure wrist thickness with caliper at the maximum joint diameter of the wrist/front paw.
Measure ankle thickness with caliper at the maximum joint diameter of the ankle/back paw.
Grip the mouse by its proximal tail.
Place the animal on a metal grasping grid, allowing only its forelimbs to grasp it.
Pull the animal backwards horizontally until it lets go of the grid.
Document the value indicated on the screen.
Repeat the measurement five times.
Calculate the mean or maximum values from the repeated measurements.
Euthanize mice according to local animal welfare guidelines.
Dissect all extremities carefully.
Strip left side limbs of all muscle and soft tissue.
Separate wrist, ankle, and knee joints.
Leave joint capsules intact.
Snap freeze joint samples in liquid nitrogen for further molecular analysis.
Strip right side limbs from skin.
Separate and fixate right side wrist, ankle, and knee joints in paraformaldehyde (PFA) 4% for 12–24 h at 4°C.
Wash out PFA and replace with PBS before micro-computed tomography (μCT) analysis.
Analyze subchondral bone areas for local changes regarding arthritis effects on bone and cartilage.
Assess wrist, ankle, and knee joints for systemic bone alterations.
Harvest blood (serum or plasma) for biomarker assessments through intracardiac puncture following euthanasia.
Extract further tissues such as muscle and visceral organs according to specific study objectives.
Store harvested tissues in PBS at 4°C for several days to weeks after PFA fixation for at least 12 h.
Store snap frozen and embedded tissues at -80°C for extended periods.
